title: open-audio-fetch source catalog
description: The contract every entry in catalog.json must satisfy. This is what a contributor's PR is validated against — both by `open-audio-fetch --validate-catalog` and in CI. The legality fields are mandatory: a source belongs in this index only if it offers audio for free and its terms/robots permit fetching.

_about.description: Human-facing legend and provenance; not validated per-key.

id.description: Stable slug; also the CLI argument if an adapter exists.

license.description: The prevailing license posture of the source.

license_url.description: REQUIRED. Page stating the rights (a license URL, a PD statement, or the section of terms granting free download).

terms_url.description: Site terms of service, if distinct from license_url.

personal_use.description: Must be true — free personal use is the baseline for inclusion.

redistributable.description: May a downloader legally re-share the content? yes=PD/CC0/CC-BY; conditional=CC with NC/SA/ND terms; no=personal-listening only (e.g. podcasts); mixed=varies per item.

robots_ok.description: Whether robots.txt / API terms permit the fetching this project does. Must be true to ship an active adapter.

robots.description: Human note on the robots/terms posture.

check_url.description: Canonical URL `--doctor` should probe for robots + reachability — the endpoint we actually fetch (e.g. the API host), not the marketing homepage. Falls back to `url` when absent.

added_by.description: Contributor handle (e.g. 'core' or a GitHub username).

verified.description: ISO date a maintainer last confirmed the license/robots claim.
